scenario: A startup wants to avoid buying servers up front and pay only for the computing it uses. Which cloud benefit is this?

options.text: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Go global in minutes with Regions

explanation: Pay-as-you-go replaces large up-front capital expense (CapEx) with ongoing operating expense (OpEx).

scenario: A retailer's traffic spikes every holiday season. Which cloud benefit lets it avoid buying servers for peak load all year?

options.text: Benefit from massive economies of scale

options.note: Related, but the question is about sizing.

explanation: Scale out for the peak and back in afterward instead of overprovisioning.

scenario: Why can AWS often offer lower prices than a company running its own data center?

options.note: Data transfer out is usually charged.

explanation: Aggregated usage from many customers lets AWS buy and operate at lower cost per unit.

scenario: A company wants to launch its app for customers in Asia without building new data centers. Which benefit applies?
explanation: Deploy to AWS Regions around the world in minutes.

scenario: Which describes elasticity in the cloud?

options.text: Automatically adding and removing resources to match demand
Keeping copies of data in three separate locations
Paying for capacity in advance to get a discount

explanation: Elasticity scales resources out and in as load changes; Auto Scaling is a common example.

scenario: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on recovering from failures and meeting demand?
explanation: Reliability covers fault tolerance, recovery and scaling to meet demand.

scenario: Which Well-Architected pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of workloads?
explanation: The six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability.

scenario: Which Well-Architected pillar includes running workloads, monitoring them and making small, frequent, reversible changes?
explanation: Operations as code, frequent small changes and learning from failures are key principles.

scenario: A team selects the right EC2 instance types and uses caching to meet latency goals. Which Well-Architected pillar is this?
explanation: Performance efficiency is about using computing resources efficiently as demand changes.

scenario: Which Well-Architected pillar includes analyzing spending and removing unused resources?
explanation: Adopt a consumption model and measure overall efficiency.

scenario: Which tool reviews a workload against AWS best practices and highlights high-risk issues?
explanation: The Well-Architected Tool is free in the console and uses the framework's questions.

scenario: Which design principle recommends building systems that keep working if one component fails?
explanation: Use multiple Availability Zones, loose coupling and automatic recovery.

scenario: Which principle describes breaking an application into components that communicate through queues so one failure doesn't stop the others?

options.note: Components depend directly on each other.

explanation: Amazon SQS is a common way to decouple components.

scenario: Which migration strategy moves an application to AWS without changes?

options.note: Moves to a different product, like SaaS.

explanation: The 7 Rs: retire, retain, rehost, relocate, repurchase, replatform and refactor.

scenario: A company moves its database to Amazon RDS with minor changes, but doesn't redesign the app. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Replatform (lift, tinker and shift) gains some cloud benefits with small changes.

scenario: A company replaces its on-premises CRM with a SaaS product. Which migration strategy is this?

options.note: Small changes to the same app.

explanation: Repurchase means moving to a different product, often a SaaS license.

scenario: A company decides to keep some apps in its data center for now because they're not ready to move. Which strategy is this?
explanation: Retain (revisit) keeps workloads where they are until later.

scenario: A company redesigns a monolithic app into serverless microservices. Which migration strategy is this?
explanation: Refactor (re-architect) costs the most effort but gains the most cloud benefits.

scenario: Which framework helps organizations plan their cloud adoption across perspectives like Business, People and Governance?
explanation: CAF perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security and Operations.

scenario: Which AWS CAF perspective focuses on culture, training and organizational change?
explanation: The Business, People and Governance perspectives focus on business capabilities.

scenario: Which AWS CAF perspective focuses on building the cloud architecture and infrastructure?
explanation: Platform, Security and Operations are the technical perspectives.

scenario: Which is a benefit of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework?

options.text: Free EC2 instances for a year

options.note: CAF is guidance, not a tool.

explanation: CAF lists reduced business risk, improved ESG performance, increased revenue and increased operational efficiency.

scenario: Which service helps move on-premises servers to AWS by continuously replicating them?
explanation: Application Migration Service is the main tool for rehosting servers.

scenario: Which service migrates a database to AWS while the source stays operational?
explanation: DMS supports homogeneous and heterogeneous migrations; Schema Conversion helps change engines.

scenario: Which concept means a company only pays for compute while its code actually runs?

options.note: Pay for a whole physical server.

explanation: AWS Lambda charges per request and execution time.

scenario: Which deployment model connects on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources?

options.note: Multiple AWS Regions, not on premises.

explanation: Hybrid examples include AWS Outposts, Direct Connect and Site-to-Site VPN.

scenario: Which is an advantage of the cloud's economies of scale for customers?
explanation: AWS has reduced prices many times as it has grown.

scenario: A company wants to experiment with new ideas quickly and shut down failed experiments at low cost. Which benefit applies?
explanation: New resources are a click away, so experiments are cheap and fast.

scenario: Which describes the cloud's total cost of ownership (TCO) advantage?

options.text: Lower costs for hardware, power and staff
Free software licenses for all apps

explanation: TCO compares all costs: servers, storage, network, power, cooling, space and labor.

scenario: Under the shared responsibility model, which task is the customer's responsibility for Amazon EC2?
explanation: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud; customers are responsible for security IN the cloud.

scenario: Under the shared responsibility model, which is AWS's responsibility?
explanation: AWS manages the hardware, software, networking and facilities that run AWS services.

scenario: Which is a shared control between AWS and the customer?
explanation: AWS patches infrastructure; customers patch their guest OS and apps. Configuration management and awareness training are also shared.

scenario: For a managed service like Amazon RDS, who patches the database engine?

options.note: Patching is part of the service.

explanation: With managed services, AWS takes on more responsibility. Customers still manage access and data.

scenario: Which AWS account identity has complete access and should be used only for a few account tasks?
explanation: Protect the root user with MFA and don't use it for everyday tasks.

scenario: What is the best practice for protecting the root user?

options.text: Enable MFA and lock away its credentials
Share it with the whole admin team
Create long-term access keys for it

explanation: Use IAM users, roles or IAM Identity Center for daily work.

scenario: Which task requires signing in as the root user?
explanation: Other root-only tasks include changing account settings like the root email and restoring IAM admin permissions.

scenario: Which principle grants users only the permissions they need to do their job?
explanation: Start with minimal permissions and add more as needed.

scenario: An EC2 instance needs to read objects from S3. What's the most secure way to give it access?

options.text: Attach an IAM role to the instance
Store access keys on the instance

explanation: Roles provide temporary credentials that rotate automatically.

scenario: Which IAM feature groups users so they share the same permissions?

options.note: Assumed temporarily, not a collection of users.

explanation: Attach policies to groups rather than to individual users.

scenario: Which document defines permissions in IAM?
explanation: Policies list Effect, Action, Resource and optional Conditions.

scenario: Which service provides single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts and business apps for a workforce?
explanation: IAM Identity Center can connect to an existing identity provider like Microsoft Entra ID.

scenario: Which service adds sign-up and sign-in to a customer-facing mobile app?
explanation: Cognito supports social sign-in and user pools.

scenario: A company with many AWS accounts wants to block all accounts from using certain Regions. What should it use?

options.text: Service control policies in AWS Organizations
IAM user policies in each account

explanation: SCPs set maximum permissions for accounts in an organization.

scenario: Where can a customer download AWS compliance reports such as SOC and ISO certifications?
explanation: Artifact also lets you review and accept agreements such as a BAA.

scenario: Which service records API calls made in an AWS account for auditing?
explanation: CloudTrail answers who did what, when and from where.

scenario: Which service tracks resource configuration changes and checks them against rules?
explanation: Config rules can flag noncompliant resources, like unencrypted volumes.

scenario: Which service uses machine learning to detect threats like unusual API calls or compromised instances?
explanation: GuardDuty analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs.

scenario: Which service automatically scans EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities?
explanation: Inspector also scans Lambda functions.

scenario: Which service discovers personally identifiable information (PII) stored in Amazon S3?
explanation: Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to find sensitive data.

scenario: Which service gives a combined view of security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie?
explanation: Security Hub also runs automated security best-practice checks.

scenario: Which service helps investigate the root cause of a security finding using graphs of related activity?
explanation: Detective builds a linked view from logs to speed up investigations.

scenario: Which service protects all AWS customers from common DDoS attacks at no extra cost?

options.note: Paid, with extra protections and response team.

explanation: Shield Advanced adds cost protection and access to the Shield Response Team.

scenario: A company wants to block SQL injection and cross-site scripting requests to its web app. What should it use?
explanation: WAF works with CloudFront, Application Load Balancer and API Gateway.

scenario: Which service creates and manages encryption keys used by many AWS services?
explanation: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules if needed.

scenario: Which service stores database passwords and can rotate them automatically?
explanation: Systems Manager Parameter Store can also hold configuration data and secrets.

scenario: Which service provides free public TLS certificates for use with load balancers and CloudFront?
explanation: ACM renews its certificates automatically.

scenario: Which acts as a stateful firewall for an EC2 instance?

options.note: Connects a VPC to the internet.

explanation: Security groups allow rules only; return traffic is automatically allowed.

scenario: Which is true of network ACLs?

options.text: They're stateless and apply to subnets
They're stateful and apply to instances

explanation: Because they're stateless, return traffic must be explicitly allowed.

scenario: Who is responsible for encrypting data stored in Amazon S3 for a specific compliance need?

options.note: AWS provides tools; customers choose settings.

explanation: S3 encrypts new objects by default, but customers decide on key management to meet their requirements.

scenario: Which describes data encryption in transit?

options.text: Protecting data as it moves over a network
Protecting data stored on a disk
Copying data to another Region for backup

explanation: TLS (HTTPS) is the most common way to encrypt data in transit.

scenario: What's the main benefit of requiring multi-factor authentication (MFA) in AWS?

options.text: Stolen passwords alone can't sign in
Users no longer need any passwords
It encrypts all data stored in S3

explanation: Use virtual authenticator apps, passkeys or hardware security keys.

scenario: Which IAM tool shows when a user's credentials were last used, to help remove unused ones?
explanation: IAM Access Analyzer can also find unused access and resources shared outside the account.

scenario: Which service sends alerts when a CloudWatch metric crosses a threshold, such as high CPU?
explanation: Alarms can notify through Amazon SNS or trigger Auto Scaling.

scenario: Which service provides managed Microsoft Active Directory in AWS?
explanation: AWS Managed Microsoft AD can trust an on-premises domain.

scenario: What is an AWS Region?

options.text: A geographic area with multiple Availability Zones

options.note: That's closer to an AZ's building.

options.text: A cache location for the CDN network

explanation: Choose Regions based on compliance, latency, service availability and price.

scenario: What is an Availability Zone?

options.text: One or more data centers with separate power and networking
A caching site used by CloudFront

explanation: AZs in a Region are connected with low-latency links but isolated from each other's failures.

scenario: How can an application be made highly available within a Region?

options.text: Deploy it across multiple Availability Zones
Use a single, larger EC2 instance
options.note: Still a single point of failure.

options.text: Use one AZ with nightly backups

explanation: Use a load balancer to spread traffic across instances in several AZs.

scenario: Which factor is NOT usually a reason for choosing an AWS Region?

options.text: The number of IAM users needed

explanation: IAM is global, so it doesn't depend on the Region. Pricing also differs between Regions.

scenario: What are edge locations used for?
explanation: CloudFront, Route 53 and Global Accelerator use the edge network.

scenario: Which service runs AWS infrastructure in a customer's own data center?
explanation: Outposts suits low-latency or data-residency needs on premises.

scenario: Which AWS infrastructure places compute close to large cities for single-digit millisecond latency?
explanation: Local Zones extend a parent Region to metro areas.

scenario: Which service provides resizable virtual servers in the cloud?
explanation: Choose instance families for general purpose, compute, memory, storage or accelerated workloads.

scenario: Which service runs code without servers in response to events, billed per request and duration?
explanation: Lambda functions can run for up to 15 minutes.

scenario: Which service runs containers without managing servers or clusters of EC2 instances?
explanation: Fargate works with Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS.

scenario: Which service runs Kubernetes clusters managed by AWS?
explanation: Amazon ECR is the registry for container images.

scenario: A developer wants to upload code and have AWS handle deployment, load balancing and scaling. Which service fits?
explanation: You still have control of the underlying resources if needed.

scenario: Which service offers simple virtual servers with a predictable monthly price for small websites?
explanation: Lightsail bundles compute, storage and data transfer.

scenario: Which service automatically adds or removes EC2 instances based on demand?
explanation: Auto Scaling also replaces unhealthy instances.

scenario: Which service distributes incoming traffic across multiple EC2 instances?
explanation: Application Load Balancers route HTTP; Network Load Balancers handle TCP/UDP.

scenario: Which storage service stores any amount of data as objects in buckets?
explanation: S3 Standard is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability.

scenario: Which S3 storage class is lowest cost for archives that are rarely accessed and can wait hours to retrieve?
explanation: Deep Archive retrievals typically take up to 12 hours (or 48 for bulk).

scenario: A company has data with unknown or changing access patterns. Which S3 class moves data automatically to save cost?
explanation: Intelligent-Tiering has no retrieval fees.

scenario: Which storage is a block-level volume attached to a single EC2 instance and persists after stopping it?
explanation: EBS volumes live in one AZ; use snapshots to back them up.

scenario: Which storage provides a shared file system that many Linux EC2 instances can mount at once?
explanation: Amazon FSx offers Windows File Server, Lustre and other file systems.

scenario: Which service connects on-premises applications to cloud storage using a local appliance or VM?
explanation: Modes include S3 File Gateway, FSx File Gateway, Volume Gateway and Tape Gateway.

scenario: Which service centrally manages and automates backups across AWS services?
explanation: Backup plans set schedules and retention.

scenario: Which managed relational database service supports engines like MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server?
explanation: Multi-AZ deployments add a standby for high availability.

scenario: Which AWS-built relational database is compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL and offers higher performance?
explanation: Aurora stores six copies of data across three AZs.

scenario: Which serverless NoSQL database provides single-digit millisecond performance at any scale?
explanation: DynamoDB is a key-value and document database.

scenario: Which service is a data warehouse for running analytics queries on large datasets?
explanation: Redshift Serverless runs analytics without managing clusters.

scenario: Which service adds an in-memory cache to speed up database reads?
explanation: ElastiCache supports Valkey, Redis OSS and Memcached.

scenario: Which service creates a logically isolated virtual network in AWS?
explanation: VPCs contain public and private subnets, route tables and gateways.

scenario: Which component lets resources in a public subnet reach the internet?
explanation: A route to the internet gateway makes a subnet public.

scenario: Which service provides a dedicated private network connection from on premises to AWS?
explanation: Direct Connect offers consistent performance; VPN is faster to set up.

scenario: Which service is a scalable DNS service that can route users based on latency or health?
explanation: Routing policies include simple, weighted, latency, failover and geolocation.

scenario: Which service delivers website content with low latency using a global network of edge locations?
explanation: CloudFront can serve content from S3, load balancers or other origins.

scenario: Which service decouples application components using a message queue?
explanation: Messages wait in the queue until a consumer processes them.

scenario: Which service sends notifications to many subscribers, such as email, SMS and Lambda, at once?
explanation: SNS uses a publish/subscribe model with topics.

scenario: Which service defines AWS infrastructure as code using templates?
explanation: The AWS CDK lets you define infrastructure in programming languages.

scenario: Which service helps manage and patch fleets of EC2 instances and on-premises servers?
explanation: Features include Patch Manager, Session Manager and Run Command.

scenario: Which service queries data in S3 using standard SQL without loading it into a database?
explanation: Athena is serverless and charges per data scanned.

scenario: Which service creates interactive business intelligence dashboards?
explanation: QuickSight can use data from Athena, Redshift, RDS and more.

scenario: Which service collects and processes real-time streaming data, such as clickstreams?
explanation: Amazon Data Firehose can load streams into S3, Redshift and more.

scenario: Which service lets developers build and train their own machine learning models?
explanation: Pre-built AI services need no ML expertise; SageMaker AI is for custom models.

scenario: Which service analyzes images and videos to detect objects and faces?
explanation: Other AI services: Polly (speech), Transcribe (speech to text), Translate and Comprehend.

scenario: Which service gives access to foundation models from several providers through one API for generative AI apps?
explanation: Amazon Q is a generative AI assistant for business and developers.

scenario: A workload runs steadily 24/7 for the next three years. Which EC2 pricing option is typically cheapest?
explanation: Commitments of 1 or 3 years give discounts of up to 72% compared with On-Demand.

scenario: A batch job can be stopped and restarted at any time. Which EC2 option offers the biggest discount?
explanation: Spot uses spare capacity at up to 90% off, with a two-minute interruption notice.

scenario: A team is testing a new app for a few weeks and doesn't know how long it'll run. Which pricing option fits?
explanation: On-Demand has no commitment and bills per second for most Linux instances.

scenario: Which pricing option commits to a dollar amount per hour of compute and applies to EC2, Fargate and Lambda?
explanation: Compute Savings Plans are flexible across instance families and Regions.

scenario: A company must use its existing per-socket software licenses on physical servers. Which option fits?
explanation: Dedicated Hosts give visibility into sockets and cores.

scenario: Which is generally free in AWS?

options.text: Data transfer into AWS from the internet
Data transfer out to the internet

explanation: Data transfer between AZs and out to the internet is usually charged.

scenario: Which tool estimates the cost of a planned AWS architecture before deployment?
explanation: Estimates can be shared with a link.

scenario: Which tool visualizes past AWS spending and forecasts future costs?
explanation: Cost Explorer can filter by service, account and tag.

scenario: A company wants an email alert when monthly spend is forecast to exceed $1,000. What should it use?
explanation: Budgets can also trigger actions, like applying an IAM policy.

scenario: Which feature helps track costs by project or department?
explanation: Activate tags in the Billing console to see them in reports.

scenario: Which feature gives a single bill for many AWS accounts and can combine usage for volume discounts?
explanation: Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts can be shared across accounts.

scenario: Which tool provides the most detailed, line-item cost and usage data for analysis?

options.text: AWS Cost and Usage Reports (Data Exports)

explanation: Reports are delivered to an S3 bucket and can be queried with Athena.

scenario: Which service recommends right-sized EC2 instances based on usage history?
explanation: Trusted Advisor and Cost Explorer also offer rightsizing guidance.

scenario: Which service checks an account for cost savings, security gaps, fault tolerance and service limits?
explanation: Basic Support includes core checks; paid plans unlock the full set.

scenario: Which AWS Support plan is free for every account?
explanation: Basic includes billing support, documentation, re:Post, Health Dashboard and core Trusted Advisor checks.

scenario: Which AWS Support plan includes a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM)?
explanation: As of 2026, AWS is moving Developer and Business customers to Business Support+, and Enterprise On-Ramp to Enterprise, by January 2027.

scenario: Which resource offers free answers to AWS questions from the community and AWS experts?
explanation: AWS Knowledge Center articles answer common questions.

scenario: Where can a customer buy third-party software, such as firewalls, that runs on AWS?
explanation: Marketplace offers free trials, hourly and annual pricing.

scenario: A company needs help from a consulting firm to migrate to AWS. Which program helps find one?
explanation: AWS Professional Services is AWS's own consulting team.

scenario: Which shows the status of AWS services and events that affect a customer's own resources?
explanation: AWS Health gives personalized alerts about scheduled maintenance and outages.

scenario: Who should a customer contact for help with a billing question?
explanation: Account and billing support cases are included even with Basic Support.

scenario: Which factor affects Amazon S3 storage costs?

options.text: The number of VPCs in the account

explanation: Requests and data transfer out also affect S3 costs.

scenario: What's the main cost benefit of turning off development EC2 instances outside working hours?

options.text: You stop paying for compute while stopped

explanation: Instance Scheduler on AWS can automate start and stop times.

scenario: Which pricing option needs no commitment but can be reclaimed by AWS with a two-minute warning?
explanation: Use Spot for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads.
